provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2029-07-26T07 UTC: the Sun's centre is 0.59 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 3.00 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 95%, Earth in view 86%, both 82% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 151 Wh).
Longest darkness 16 h: that is the cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 549 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Darkest spell from 2029-08-05T03 UTC (16 h): terrain 8.9 km away blocks it (bearing 24 deg: skyline 1.54 deg, centre of the body at 1.20 deg).
Longest Earth blackout from 2029-08-07T09 UTC (46 h): it is below the Moon's own curvature (bearing 146 deg, horizon -0.28 deg).
